observations.text_description: ~0.23 mM monomers from bean cake pc-PET at 50 C, 24 h - far lower than FAST-PETase (Fig. 3b)
~0.57 mM monomers from pretreated bottle film at 50 C, 24 h (Fig. 4c)

interactions.notes: ISF6_4831 gene product, designated PETase. Shares 51% amino acid identity and catalytic residues with the Thermobifida fusca hydrolase TfH. Transcript level during growth on PET film was the highest among all analysed coding sequences (15x, 31x and 41x that on maltose, TPA-Na and BHET respectively), indicating induction by PET film itself. Extracellular; predicted localisation in supplementary text S1.

observations.text_description: Prominent pitting developed on the PET film surface after 18 hours with 50 nM PETase at 30 degrees C, pH 7.0.
MHET (mono(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalic acid) was the major product released from PET film, together with minor amounts of TPA and BHET.

indirect_interactions.notes: Star enzyme of the study. Depolymerizes untreated postconsumer PET (51 products, water bottles, polyester textiles) and enables closed-loop PET recycling. Strong direct evidence (mass loss + HPLC monomer quantification + AFM/SEM).

observations.text_description: FAST-PETase released 6342 μM total PET monomers (TPA + MHET) from Gf-PET film after 72 h at 55 °C, pH 9.0. Read from Fig. 5.

Residual activity of FAST-PETase fell to 50 % of its own initial activity after approximately 48 h of pre-incubation at 55 °C - the half-life reported by the authors, estimated from the residual-activity decay curve in Fig. 5f.

variants.description: Functional, active, stable and tolerant PETase: five mutations vs WT PETase (S121E/D186H/R224Q/N233K/R280A). Highest overall PET-hydrolytic activity at 30-50 C of all enzymes tested; degrades untreated postconsumer PET completely within 1 week at 50 C.
variants.performance: At 40 and 50 C, 2.4- and 38-fold higher activity than ThermoPETase; releases 33.8 mM PET monomers from amorphous gf-PET in 96 h at 50 C (highest of all mutants/temperatures tested).

experiment.notes: Inverse Michaelis-Menten analysis (Baath et al. formalism) over 2 h, pH 8, 50 degC, 50 mg PET in 5 mL. IMPORTANT: the reported constant is the INVERSE Michaelis constant - the molar ENZYME concentration at half-saturation of the substrate surface - not a classical substrate Km. It is stored in kinetics.km because the contract has no separate field for it; a lower value means higher enzyme-substrate affinity. Fast-PETase.
